answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate combined with the incumbent's refusal to reopen pricing creates a hard constraint. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing—precisely the cost outcome needed. However, the 94% utilization buffer and 14-day renewal deadline introduce delivery risk. Verify memory_c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor's onboarding speed and reliability metrics can be replicated under time pressure. memory_c4 and memory_c6 show negotiation and multi-year commitments both failed to meet the 18% threshold; deferral (memory_c5) buys time but wastes the renewal window and leaves the line exposed month-to-month. A standard experiment switch minimizes total cost of ownership by meeting the mandate while accepting elevated short-term delivery risk that can be mitigated through phased volume transfer and parallel supply staging during the transition window.
